headline: Endorsed bid waivers for E-J Electric Installation Co., McPhee Electric Ltd. and AT&T cellular service.
summary: Commissioners approved the Director's Report for September 2026 and the minutes of October 6, 2026. Staff also discussed a planned 115-kV circuit breaker at the Wallingford 13M Substation, estimated at around $5,000,000.00 and expected to add about 36 MW of contingency rating. The Director said FERC might act on ISO rulemaking probably January 1st or later.
decisions: Approved the Director's Report for September 2026, 3-0.
Endorsed a bid waiver for E-J Electric Installation Co. to do emergency work if needed, 3-0.
Endorsed a bid waiver for McPhee Electric Ltd. to do emergency work if needed, 3-0.
Endorsed a bid waiver for AT&T cellular services, provided they are the lowest cost and meet technical requirements, 3-0.

45 Dr. Rinebold requested an update from Mr. Hendershot in regards to the matters pertaining to 
46 ISO rulemaking. 
47 
48 Mr. Hendershot stated that he attended a mini conference /training hosted by NEP P A and 
49 presented by Energy New England, as well as a third-party consultant who works for NEPOOL 
50 and a representative from MWEEC. Mr. Hendershot learned that things are moving along and 
51 that the filings are at FERC to make the changes that the internal market monitor had proposed. 
52 Mr. Hendershot stated that this is fast for these entities to get these changes in place.

58 Dr. Rinebold requested an update from Mr. Arborio in regards to the addition of a 115-kV circuit 
59 breaker at the Wallingford 13M Substation . 
60 
61 Mr. Arborio stated that currently the Wallingford 13M Substation has a contingency rating of 86 
62 MW that is limited by the A 1 bus which isolates the 2X and 3X transformers . It has been 
63 suggested to install the 13M 8T breaker to split the bus effectively and isolate those two 
64 transfonners in order to increase the contingency rating of 13M Substation by approximately 
65 36MW. Last FY, the WED ordered a replacement 115-kVcircuit breaker for the Colony 50E 
66 Substation due to obsolescence. At that time, the lead time for these breakers was two to three 
67 years. In addition to this there will need to be reconstruction done to the distribution bus. This 
68 will give the WED a contingency rating increase of about 36 MW and buy the WED some 
69 significant time to design, expand and increase the capacity of both North Wallingford and 
70 Wallingford Substation. The installation of the breaker that the WED is proposing would need to 
71 be done in either case. The total estimated cost is around $5,000,000.00 and is pretty volatile 
72 especially with the latest executive orders. If the WED gets the declaratory ruling and goes 
73 through Town Council relatively quickly , the duration of the design and construction is a year . 
74 
75 Dr. Rinebold commented that this is a good thoughtful approach and good work . 
76 
77 Mr. Zabrowski commented that he is glad that the WED is looking ahead and getting these out of 
78 the way. This is good planning . 
79

96 5. Discussion and Possible Action: Bid Waiver Request - Electric Division - E-J 
97 Electric Installation Co. 
98 
99 Mr. Arborio stated that the WED is seeking the PUC to endorse a bid waiver to allow the 
100 Division to utilize E-J Electric Installation Co. of Wallingford, CT. The WED is in the process of 
101 creating an emergency response plan and at present, its current model is to utilize the NEPPA 
102 mutual assistance portal to contact participating utilities in the e\ent of a storm or any other 
103 systemic need for utility construction activities. During these times, it is common for the 
104 surrounding utilities to be burdened with damage as well, thus straining their staffing and 
105 hindering their ability to assist when the WED needs it most. To provide flexibi lity and diversity 
106 in times of need , the WED requests a bid-waiver with E-J Electric Co. for the remainder of the 
107 fiscal year. E-J Electric cUlTently resides in Wallingford and has performed work within the 
108 Wallingford Electric system . They have been in business since the twenties and are the ninth 
109 largest contractor in the company . It was noted that it is the same situation with McPhee Electric, 
110 Ltd. for item #6 whereas the WED is looking to allow McPhee Electric , Ltd. to provide services 
111 in times of need for the remainder of the fiscal year. 
112 
113 Mr. Hendershot stated that realistically, what happens in events like these are if the systems have 
114 contractors on the property and the other systems do not need them, they will release them to go 
115 wherever they may go. The WED typically does not have contractors on the system . The WED 
116 would like to put something in place so the WED can have a relationship with these firms and 
117 get these resources when they are needed. Mr. Hendershot noted the actual process for the PUC 
118 is to endorse the request for a bid waiver not to approve the bid waiver as the Town Council does 
119 that. 
120 
121 Motion to: Endorse a Bid Waiver to allow E-J Electric Installation Co. to perform work in 
122 compliance with the Wallingford Electric Division Emergency Response Plan if and as 
123 needed for the remainder of the fiscal year.

144 7. Discussion and Possible Action: Bid Waiver Request - Electric Division - AT&T 
145 Cellular Plan 
146 
147 Mr. Arborio stated that periodically, the WED evalu ates its recurring mobile phone plan to 
148 ensure that it receives the most cost-effe ctive solution . In addition to the cellular component , it 
149 was discovered that the copper phone line within the 100 John Street facility was not going to be 
150 supported , which feeds the WED ' s fax lines . This will now need to be transitioned to a cellular 
151 option as well. An analysis was carried out between AT&T , Verizon and the WED ' s current 
152 provider , T-Mobile. It was found that including the on-site requirements, AT&T was the least 
153 costl y supplier who could provide service meeting the WED's requirements. In addition , AT&T 
154 has strong emer gency /outage support capabilities including temporary loaner phones , aerial 
155 signal support and vehicle-based signal booster units should a widespread power outage occur . 
156 Frontier who is now Verizon, is no longer offering copper lines to their customers. While there 
157 will be an initial cost incurred to transition to the new hardware, RO t will be reflected within 
158 11.2 months. This waiver shall replace the existing T-Mobile bid waiver once all charges have 
159 been paid. This will get the WED 25 iPhones , 15 iPads and a signal booster for the building . 
160 
161 Mr. Hendershot questioned if this has been reviewed with the Purchasing Bureau? 
162 
163 Mr. Arborio responded absol utely. 
164 
165 Dr. Rinebold stated that the analysis looks good and that he is very supportive of low cost with 
166 the company that can meet the WED's needs. Dr. Rinebold questioned how will the WED know 
167 if these numbers wi II be valid going into the future ? Are these hard prices? 
168 
169 Mr. Arborio stated that these are hard the prices that came from them directl y. 
170 
171 There was some discussion and clarification by Mr. Hendershot in regard to the above given to 
172 the member of the public in attendance .
